title: Canonical isomorphism between pullback functors for two maps over a base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $a:X\to S$ and $b:T\to S$ be morphisms, and let $r_0,r_1:T\to X$ be morphisms over $S$. Pullback of descent data [def-pd-descent-datum] along $r_0$ and along $r_1$ gives canonically naturally isomorphic functors $DD(X/S)\to DD(T/S)$. More generally, for morphisms $r:T\to X$ and $t:U\to T$ over $S$, the pullback functor along $r\circ t$ is canonically naturally isomorphic to the composite of the pullback functors along $r$ and $t$, using the canonical associativity isomorphism $U\times_T(T\times_X V)\cong U\times_X V$ of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Here $DD(X/S)$ denotes the category whose objects are the descent data $(V,\varphi)$ on schemes $V$ over $X$ relative to $X/S$ [def-pd-descent-datum] and whose morphisms $(V,\varphi)\to(W,\psi)$ are the morphisms $\alpha:V\to W$ over $X$ with $\psi\circ\mathrm{pr}_0^*\alpha=\mathrm{pr}_1^*\alpha\circ\varphi$; for a morphism $r:T\to X$ over $S$ (with $T\to S$ the given structure map), the pullback of $(V,\varphi)$ along $r$ is $(T\times_XV,(r\times r)^*\varphi)$ [def-pc-fibre-product], where $r\times r:T\times_ST\to X\times_SX$, and the pullback of $\alpha$ is $\mathrm{id}_T\times_X\alpha$.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02VS (lemma-pullback-family), part (3), and Lemma Tag 023Y (lemma-pullback), parts (1)--(2); composition from the fibre-product construction in 023Y(1)

proof.text: For a descent datum $(V,\varphi)$ on $V\to X$, the pair $(r_0,r_1)$ is a morphism $T\to X\times_S X$ by the assumption that both maps are over $S$. Pulling the isomorphism $\varphi:\mathrm{pr}_0^*V\cong\mathrm{pr}_1^*V$ back along this pair gives an isomorphism $T\times_{X,r_0}V\cong T\times_{X,r_1}V$ over $T$. The universal property and functoriality of fibre products make this construction natural in $(V,\varphi)$ and in morphisms of descent data, so it defines a natural isomorphism between the two pullback functors.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 023Y (lemma-pullback), part (2) and its proof (the map r: X' -> X x_S X); family version Tag 02VS (lemma-pullback-family), part (3)

proof.text: The isomorphism in Step 1 is an isomorphism of descent data over $T/S$: after pulling it back to $T\times_ST$ and then to $T\times_ST\times_ST$, both possible composites are the pullback of the two sides of the cocycle identity for $\varphi$. Thus the equality required of a morphism in $DD(T/S)$ follows from the cocycle condition in the definition of descent datum, and the inverse gives the inverse morphism.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 023Y (lemma-pullback), part (2) and its proof (the map r: X' -> X x_S X); family version Tag 02VS (lemma-pullback-family), part (3)

proof.text: For morphisms $r:T\to X$ and $t:U\to T$ over $S$, the pullback along $r\circ t$ has underlying scheme $U\times_XV$, while the iterated pullback has underlying scheme $U\times_T(T\times_XV)$. The universal property of fibre products gives the canonical associativity isomorphism $U\times_T(T\times_XV)\cong U\times_XV$; functoriality identifies the pulled-back descent data and morphisms under this isomorphism. These identifications are natural and yield the asserted canonical natural isomorphism of functors.
